title: Context and Quality Regression Triage
summary: Isolate whether an AI quality regression comes from task distribution, prompts, context, retrieval, model behavior, tools, graders, or application changes.
prerequisites: A versioned baseline and representative evaluation set
Traceable prompt, context, retrieval, model, tool, and grader versions
A privacy-approved path for sampling production-shaped failures

sections.title: Freeze the observation before changing the system
paragraphs: Capture a privacy-safe reproducer and the exact application, prompt, policy, context recipe, retrieval corpus and index, model, parameters, tools, grader, dependency, and deployment versions. Compare the same case against the last verified baseline. Do not change prompt, model, context, retrieval, and grader together; one-at-a-time experiments preserve causal evidence.

Classify the first divergence as task-distribution shift, missing or stale context, retrieval miss, conflicting evidence, context truncation, instruction collision, prompt regression, model behavior change, tool trajectory change, parser or post-processing defect, grader drift, or telemetry defect. Inspect critical slices and individual severe failures because an average can remain stable while one population or use case regresses.

sections.title: Create a regression comparison record
paragraphs: Keep source and candidate runs under equivalent conditions and record unavoidable differences. Turn a confirmed failure into a governed regression case with provenance, expected and forbidden outcomes, and retention controls. If the affected content is time-sensitive, reverify authoritative sources rather than teaching the model to repeat stale text.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the minimized case, exact versions, first divergent transition, controlled comparisons, slice-level metrics, source freshness, root-cause confidence, containment, owner, and a durable regression test. Verify the proposed fix against the failing case, full representative set, critical safety and accessibility slices, grader calibration, latency, cost, and a production-shaped smoke test.

Stop rollout when a blocking safety or privacy case fails, a critical slice crosses its threshold, baseline and candidate conditions are not comparable, evidence is stale, telemetry is unreliable, or the cause remains unknown at consequential scale. Recovery means restoring the last verified component set or disabling the affected route, invalidating misleading results, rebuilding context or indexes when required, and promoting only after the unchanged gate passes.
sections.callout: A prompt edit is not a diagnosis; isolate the first changed contract.

sections.title: Worked simulation: complete documents, versions, and trace boundary
paragraphs: This bounded, provider-neutral simulation replays authored observations with fictional, privacy-safe documents and exact recorded strings. It is not a real model evaluation, a measurement of any provider capability, or proof of a production fix. It uses no customer data, network service, secret, production telemetry, or production write.

The original operating goal is preserved: answer benefits-support questions only from the supplied documents, route accessibility requests correctly, avoid inventing fees, deadlines, eligibility rules, or approval outcomes, and state when the documents do not establish an answer. The fictional sources are not authoritative policy. Their authority and freshness for any real deployment are UNKNOWN.

DOC-ACCESS-01, revision 2026-08-14, title “Accessible appointment requests.” Full authored text: “To request an appointment in an accessible format, contact the Access Desk through the member portal by selecting Access support, or call 800-0100. Tell the Access Desk the appointment type and the format or communication support requested. The Access Desk records the request and coordinates an accessible appointment. This document does not state a fee for an accessible appointment request.”

DOC-ACCESS-02, revision 2026-08-14, title “Interpreter and alternate-format requests.” Full authored text: “A member may request an interpreter or an alternate-format copy of a bill by contacting the Access Desk through the member portal under Access support or by calling 800-0100. The member should identify the language or alternate format needed and the document concerned. The Access Desk records the request and coordinates the request. This document does not state a 24-hour deadline and does not say that an interpreter is unavailable.”

DOC-BILL-01, revision 2026-08-14, title “Routine billing disputes.” Full authored text: “For a routine billing error, contact Billing Services through the member portal under Billing questions or call 800-0200. Include the bill date, disputed item, and explanation. Billing Services reviews the dispute and responds. This document does not say that an appeal is automatically approved.”

DOC-PLAN-01, revision 2026-08-14, title “Plan change notice.” Full authored text: “For a plan change, the member receives a notice describing the change and its stated effective date. The notice is the source for the applicable effective date. This document does not say that every plan change takes effect immediately.”

The authored corpus is corpus-benefits-2026-08-14. The baseline is app benefits-assistant-2.7.0, prompt policy-answer-v1.2, context recipe context-pack-4.1, corpus corpus-benefits-2026-08-14, retrieval index index-3.3, model record provider-neutral-model-recorded-2026-08-01, parameters params-17, tools none, grader rubric-2.0, dependencies lock-2026-08-10, and deployment deploy-441. The candidate keeps every listed component unchanged except retrieval index-3.4 and deployment deploy-447.

The procedure is: freeze the documents, cases, versions, outputs, and scoring rule; replay baseline and candidate observations; compare aggregate and critical-slice results; inspect the first trace divergence; change one component at a time; apply the immutable gate; and repeat the complete evaluation after recovery. Official evaluation guidance supports measurable criteria, baseline comparison, edge-case analysis, and multidimensional evaluation: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests. That documentation does not verify this fictional corpus, observations, thresholds, or any production result.

sections.title: Completed six-case comparison, critical slice, and immutable gate
paragraphs: Strict replay scoring marks a result as passing only when the complete result string exactly equals an entry in that case's expected list and does not equal an entry in its forbidden list. This intentionally narrow rule checks the authored fixture, not the semantic quality of arbitrary natural-language answers.

C-101 input is “How do I request an accessible appointment?” Expected: “Use DOC-ACCESS-01: request through Access support in the member portal or call 800-0100, and tell the Access Desk the appointment type and requested format or communication support.” Forbidden: “Charge an invented fee for the accessible appointment request.” Baseline and candidate retrieve and include DOC-ACCESS-01, return the expected string, and pass.

C-102 input is “How do I request an interpreter?” Expected: “Use DOC-ACCESS-02: contact Access support in the member portal or call 800-0100, identify the language needed, and ask the Access Desk to coordinate an interpreter.” Forbidden: “Tell the member that an interpreter is unavailable.” Baseline and candidate retrieve and include DOC-ACCESS-02, return the expected string, and pass. C-102 is critical.

C-103 input is “How do I request my bill in an alternate format?” Expected: “Use DOC-ACCESS-02: contact Access support in the member portal or call 800-0100, identify the alternate format and bill concerned, and ask the Access Desk to coordinate the request.” Forbidden: “Use DOC-BILL-01 and submit the alternate-format bill request within 24 hours.” Baseline retrieves and includes DOC-ACCESS-02 and returns the expected string. Candidate retrieves and includes DOC-BILL-01, omits DOC-ACCESS-02, returns the forbidden string, and fails. C-103 is critical.

C-104 input is “How do I dispute a routine billing error?” Expected: “Use DOC-BILL-01: contact Billing Services through Billing questions or call 800-0200, and include the bill date, disputed item, and explanation.” Forbidden: “The appeal is automatically approved.” Both runs retrieve and include DOC-BILL-01, return the expected string, and pass.

C-105 asks “When is a plan-change notice effective?” Expected: “Use DOC-PLAN-01: read the notice for the stated effective date.” Forbidden: “Every plan change takes effect immediately.” Both runs retrieve and include DOC-PLAN-01. Baseline returns the forbidden string and fails. Candidate returns the expected string and passes. This non-critical improvement offsets C-103 in the aggregate but does not repair the accessibility regression.

C-106 input is “What is the waiting period for an unrelated benefit?” Expected: “The supplied documents do not establish an answer.” Forbidden: “The benefit is covered under a fabricated policy.” Neither run retrieves or includes a document. Both return the expected abstention and pass. Empty retrieval and context lists are valid for this supported abstention.

The raw aggregate is baseline 5/6 and candidate 5/6. The critical slice C-102 and C-103 is baseline 2/2 and candidate 1/2. The unchanged gate requires aggregate at least 5/6, critical slice exactly 2/2, and no forbidden result in a critical case. Candidate quality is therefore BLOCKED. Overall release is also BLOCKED while quality fails. If recovery passes this quality gate, overall release becomes UNKNOWN rather than PASS because the operational gates were not evaluated.

sections.title: Independent changed-component trace task
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the next section. It is independent of C-103 and presents a different component change and trace pattern. Determine the first divergent transition, select the most specific causal key from retrieval_miss, context_truncation, prompt_regression, model_change, grader_drift, or unknown, and state what one-variable evidence supports your selection. Do not treat the observed answer alone as causal evidence.

Task input: “According to the supplied plan-change document, where should I find the applicable effective date?” The source corpus and retrieved document are unchanged. Baseline components are app benefits-assistant-2.7.0, prompt policy-answer-v1.2, context recipe context-pack-4.1, corpus corpus-benefits-2026-08-14, index index-3.3, model record provider-neutral-model-recorded-2026-08-01, parameters params-17, tools none, grader rubric-2.0, and dependencies lock-2026-08-10. The changed run differs only in context recipe context-pack-4.2-truncated.

Baseline record: retrieved ID DOC-PLAN-01; assembled context is the complete DOC-PLAN-01 text; observed result is “Use DOC-PLAN-01: read the notice for the stated effective date.” Changed record: retrieved ID DOC-PLAN-01; assembled context is the exact truncated prefix “For a plan change, the member receives a notice describing the change”; observed result is “Every plan change takes effect immediately.”

Controlled record A changes only the context recipe from context-pack-4.2-truncated back to context-pack-4.1. Retrieval remains DOC-PLAN-01, the complete document is assembled, and the observed result becomes “Use DOC-PLAN-01: read the notice for the stated effective date.” Controlled record B retains context-pack-4.2-truncated and changes only the prompt from policy-answer-v1.2 to diagnostic-prompt. Retrieval remains DOC-PLAN-01, the shortened context remains unchanged, and the observed result remains “Every plan change takes effect immediately.”

Record your answer before continuing: identify the first trace field that differs, explain why the unchanged retrieval ID is important, explain what the two controlled records do and do not establish, and give one causal key. This task supplies observations but intentionally does not provide its diagnosis or answer key.

sections.title: Specific feedback, causal keys, recovery, and repeat evaluation
paragraphs: Independent-task feedback: both runs retrieve DOC-PLAN-01, so a retrieval miss does not describe the first divergence. The first differing trace field is assembled context. The changed recipe supplies the exact truncated prefix “For a plan change, the member receives a notice describing the change” and omits the remainder of DOC-PLAN-01, including the sentences saying that the notice supplies the effective date and that changes are not always immediate. Restoring only context-pack-4.1 restores the complete evidence and expected result, while changing only the prompt leaves the shortened context and forbidden result unchanged. The most specific key for this authored task is context_truncation. This does not establish that every similar failure has that cause, nor does it test a real context window.

The six-case regression has a different diagnosis. Its index-only replay freezes the C-103 input, app, prompt, context recipe, corpus, model record, parameters, tools, grader, and dependencies. Index-3.3 retrieves and includes DOC-ACCESS-02 and returns the expected Access Desk route. Index-3.4 retrieves and includes DOC-BILL-01, omits DOC-ACCESS-02, and returns the forbidden 24-hour claim.

The C-103 prompt-only replay retains index-3.4 and its DOC-BILL-01 context. Both policy-answer-v1.2 and diagnostic-prompt return the forbidden string. Therefore, the authored C-103 causal key is retrieval_miss, with the first divergence at retrieval and context assembly. Blaming a model change is unsupported because the model record and parameters are unchanged, and changing only the index changes the retrieved evidence and result.

Containment is to restore the verified index-3.3 and deploy-441 or disable the affected route, invalidate misleading cached results, and inspect or rebuild index-3.4. Recovery evaluation must repeat all six cases, the C-102/C-103 critical slice, the controlled C-103 replay, grader calibration, privacy checks, source-authority and freshness review, latency and cost checks, telemetry checks, and a production-shaped smoke test.

The supplied offline exercise includes an authored recovery candidate using index-3.5 and deploy-448. In that changed fixture, C-103 retrieves DOC-ACCESS-02 and returns its expected string, while the other candidate observations remain passing. Its quality metrics are 6/6 aggregate and 2/2 critical. The quality gate succeeds, but the release status is UNKNOWN because operational evidence remains unknown. This is a fixture-supported success path, not a claim that index-3.5 exists in production or that a production repair succeeded.

sections.title: Offline Python 3 authored-replay exercise and validation probes
paragraphs: Save the complete file below as regression_exercise.py. It uses only the Python 3 standard library, documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/index.html. It performs no network call, model call, secret access, or production write. The exact commands are: python3 --version, python3 regression_exercise.py, and python3 -m py_compile regression_exercise.py. No package installation is required.

The validator enforces the declared four-document manifest, exact six-case manifest, exact critical membership, component-version structure, document references, retrieval/context consistency, result evidence, controlled-experiment linkage, and raw reported metrics. Empty retrieval and context lists are allowed, which is required for C-106, but those fields must still be lists containing only valid document IDs when nonempty. Expected and forbidden evidence lists must be nonempty.

Negative probes cover a missing case even after metrics are recomputed, duplicate IDs, a wrong retrieval-list type, a missing critical flag, wrong document references, mismatched controlled experiments, Boolean counts, expected/forbidden overlap, and a result unsupported by either evidence list. Each probe first validates its supplied base fixture, so it cannot pass merely by catching an unrelated pre-existing fixture error. The evaluator validates and uses its data argument rather than reading the global fixture.

The recovery test creates and validates a changed fixture, updates its versions, C-103 evidence, experiments, and metrics, and then evaluates that supplied object. This demonstrates that evaluation is not tied to the global fixture. Strict exact-string scoring remains an authored-replay mechanism rather than a natural-language evaluator.

Expected stdout, pending orchestrator execution, is exactly: aggregate baseline 5/6; aggregate candidate 5/6; critical baseline 2/2; critical candidate 1/2; observed status BLOCKED; recovery aggregate 6/6; recovery critical 2/2; recovery release UNKNOWN; negative tests passed; all assertions passed. No execution success is claimed here.

DOC_MANIFEST = {"DOC-ACCESS-01", "DOC-ACCESS-02", "DOC-BILL-01", "DOC-PLAN-01"}
CASE_FIELDS = {
    "id", "critical", "input", "expected", "forbidden", "baseline", "candidate",
    "baseline_retrieved_ids", "baseline_context_ids", "candidate_retrieved_ids", "candidate_context_ids"
}

def reject(condition, message):
    if condition:
        raise ValueError(message)

def passed(result, case):
    return result in case["expected"] and result not in case["forbidden"]

def validate_id_list(value, documents, field):
    reject(type(value) is not list, field + " must be a list")
    reject(any(type(item) is not str or not item for item in value), field + " entries must be nonempty strings")
    reject(len(value) != len(set(value)), field + " contains duplicates")
    reject(any(item not in documents for item in value), field + " references an unknown document")

def validate(data):
    reject(type(data) is not dict, "fixture must be an object")
    documents = data.get("documents")
    reject(type(documents) is not dict, "documents must be an object")
    reject(set(documents) != DOC_MANIFEST, "document manifest mismatch")
    for doc_id, doc in documents.items():
        reject(type(doc) is not dict or set(doc) != {"revision", "title", "text"}, "invalid document record: " + doc_id)
        for field in ("revision", "title", "text"):
            reject(type(doc[field]) is not str or not doc[field], "invalid document field: " + doc_id + "." + field)

    versions = data.get("versions")
    reject(type(versions) is not dict or set(versions) != {"baseline", "candidate"}, "version runs mismatch")
    for run in ("baseline", "candidate"):
        reject(type(versions[run]) is not dict or set(versions[run]) != VERSION_FIELDS, "version fields mismatch")
        reject(any(type(value) is not str or not value for value in versions[run].values()), "version values must be nonempty strings")
    for field in VERSION_FIELDS - {"index", "deployment"}:
        reject(versions["baseline"][field] != versions["candidate"][field], "unexpected changed component: " + field)

    cases = data.get("cases")
    reject(type(cases) is not list or not cases, "missing or empty cases")
    ids = []
    by_id = {}
    for case in cases:
        reject(type(case) is not dict, "case must be an object")
        reject(set(case) != CASE_FIELDS, "missing or extra case field")
        reject(type(case["id"]) is not str or not case["id"], "case id must be a nonempty string")
        reject(case["id"] in by_id, "duplicate case id")
        ids.append(case["id"])
        by_id[case["id"]] = case
        reject(type(case["critical"]) is not bool, "critical must be Boolean")
        reject(type(case["input"]) is not str or not case["input"], "input must be a nonempty string")
        for field in ("expected", "forbidden"):
            value = case[field]
            reject(type(value) is not list or not value, field + " must be a nonempty list")
            reject(any(type(item) is not str or not item for item in value), field + " entries must be nonempty strings")
            reject(len(value) != len(set(value)), field + " contains duplicates")
        reject(bool(set(case["expected"]) & set(case["forbidden"])), "expected and forbidden overlap")
        for run in ("baseline", "candidate"):
            result = case[run]
            reject(type(result) is not str or not result, run + " result must be a nonempty string")
            membership = int(result in case["expected"]) + int(result in case["forbidden"])
            reject(membership != 1, run + " result has contradictory or missing evidence")
            retrieved = run + "_retrieved_ids"
            context = run + "_context_ids"
            validate_id_list(case[retrieved], documents, retrieved)
            validate_id_list(case[context], documents, context)
            reject(case[retrieved] != case[context], run + " retrieval/context mismatch")
    reject(set(ids) != CASE_MANIFEST or len(ids) != len(CASE_MANIFEST), "case manifest mismatch")
    reject({case["id"] for case in cases if case["critical"]} != CRITICAL_MANIFEST, "critical membership mismatch")

    metrics = data.get("metrics")
    reject(type(metrics) is not dict or set(metrics) != {"aggregate", "critical"}, "metric groups mismatch")
    for group, selected in (("aggregate", cases), ("critical", [case for case in cases if case["critical"]])):
        record = metrics[group]
        reject(type(record) is not dict or set(record) != {"baseline", "candidate"}, "metric runs mismatch")
        for run in ("baseline", "candidate"):
            item = record[run]
            reject(type(item) is not dict or set(item) != {"numerator", "denominator"}, "metric record mismatch")
            numerator, denominator = item["numerator"], item["denominator"]
            reject(type(numerator) is not int or type(denominator) is not int, "counts must be integers, not Boolean")
            reject(denominator != len(selected), "denominator mismatch")
            reject(numerator < 0 or numerator > denominator, "invalid numerator")
            reject(numerator != sum(passed(case[run], case) for case in selected), "numerator mismatch")

    experiments = data.get("experiments")
    reject(type(experiments) is not dict or set(experiments) != {"index_only", "prompt_only"}, "experiment manifest mismatch")
    target = by_id["C-103"]
    index_exp = experiments["index_only"]
    prompt_exp = experiments["prompt_only"]
    for experiment in (index_exp, prompt_exp):
        reject(type(experiment) is not dict or set(experiment) != {"case_id", "runs"}, "invalid experiment")
        reject(experiment["case_id"] != "C-103", "experiment case mismatch")
        reject(type(experiment["runs"]) is not list or len(experiment["runs"]) != 2, "experiment needs two runs")
        for run in experiment["runs"]:
            reject(type(run) is not dict or set(run) != {"index", "prompt", "retrieved_ids", "context_ids", "result"}, "invalid experiment run")
            reject(type(run["index"]) is not str or not run["index"], "experiment index invalid")
            reject(type(run["prompt"]) is not str or not run["prompt"], "experiment prompt invalid")
            reject(type(run["result"]) is not str or not run["result"], "experiment result invalid")
            validate_id_list(run["retrieved_ids"], documents, "experiment retrieved_ids")
            validate_id_list(run["context_ids"], documents, "experiment context_ids")
            reject(run["retrieved_ids"] != run["context_ids"], "experiment retrieval/context mismatch")
    first, second = index_exp["runs"]
    reject(first["index"] != versions["baseline"]["index"] or second["index"] != versions["candidate"]["index"], "index experiment version mismatch")
    reject(first["index"] == second["index"] or first["prompt"] != second["prompt"], "index experiment is not one-variable")
    reject(first["prompt"] != versions["baseline"]["prompt"], "index experiment prompt mismatch")
    reject(first["retrieved_ids"] != target["baseline_retrieved_ids"] or first["context_ids"] != target["baseline_context_ids"] or first["result"] != target["baseline"], "index baseline evidence mismatch")
    reject(second["retrieved_ids"] != target["candidate_retrieved_ids"] or second["context_ids"] != target["candidate_context_ids"] or second["result"] != target["candidate"], "index candidate evidence mismatch")
    first, second = prompt_exp["runs"]
    reject(first["index"] != versions["candidate"]["index"] or second["index"] != first["index"], "prompt experiment index mismatch")
    reject(first["prompt"] != versions["candidate"]["prompt"] or second["prompt"] != "diagnostic-prompt", "prompt experiment version mismatch")
    reject(first["prompt"] == second["prompt"], "prompt experiment is not one-variable")
    for run in (first, second):
        reject(run["retrieved_ids"] != target["candidate_retrieved_ids"] or run["context_ids"] != target["candidate_context_ids"] or run["result"] != target["candidate"], "prompt experiment evidence mismatch")

def evaluate(data, run):
    validate(data)
    reject(run not in ("baseline", "candidate"), "unknown run")
    selected = data["cases"]
    critical = [case for case in selected if case["critical"]]
    return (
        (sum(passed(case[run], case) for case in selected), len(selected)),
        (sum(passed(case[run], case) for case in critical), len(critical))
    )

def release_status(data):
    aggregate, critical = evaluate(data, "candidate")
    no_forbidden_critical = all(passed(case["candidate"], case) for case in data["cases"] if case["critical"])
    quality_ok = aggregate[0] >= 5 and critical == (2, 2) and no_forbidden_critical
    return "UNKNOWN" if quality_ok else "BLOCKED"

def recompute_metrics(data):
    for group, selected in (("aggregate", data["cases"]), ("critical", [case for case in data["cases"] if case.get("critical") is True])):
        for run in ("baseline", "candidate"):
            data["metrics"][group][run] = {
                "numerator": sum(passed(case[run], case) for case in selected),
                "denominator": len(selected)
            }

def expect_reject(base, label, mutator):
    validate(base)
    changed = deepcopy(base)
    mutator(changed)
    try:
        validate(changed)
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("negative test accepted: " + label)

def make_recovery(base):
    validate(base)
    recovered = deepcopy(base)
    expected = recovered["cases"][2]["expected"][0]
    recovered["versions"]["candidate"]["index"] = "index-3.5"
    recovered["versions"]["candidate"]["deployment"] = "deploy-448"
    case = recovered["cases"][2]
    case["candidate"] = expected
    case["candidate_retrieved_ids"] = ["DOC-ACCESS-02"]
    case["candidate_context_ids"] = ["DOC-ACCESS-02"]
    index_run = recovered["experiments"]["index_only"]["runs"][1]
    index_run.update({"index": "index-3.5", "retrieved_ids": ["DOC-ACCESS-02"], "context_ids": ["DOC-ACCESS-02"], "result": expected})
    for prompt_run in recovered["experiments"]["prompt_only"]["runs"]:
        prompt_run.update({"index": "index-3.5", "retrieved_ids": ["DOC-ACCESS-02"], "context_ids": ["DOC-ACCESS-02"], "result": expected})
    recompute_metrics(recovered)
    validate(recovered)
    return recovered

def run_tests():
    validate(FIXTURE)
    aggregate_b, critical_b = evaluate(FIXTURE, "baseline")
    aggregate_c, critical_c = evaluate(FIXTURE, "candidate")
    assert aggregate_b == (5, 6) and aggregate_c == (5, 6)
    assert critical_b == (2, 2) and critical_c == (1, 2)
    assert release_status(FIXTURE) == "BLOCKED"

    recovery = make_recovery(FIXTURE)
    recovery_aggregate, recovery_critical = evaluate(recovery, "candidate")
    assert recovery_aggregate == (6, 6) and recovery_critical == (2, 2)
    assert release_status(recovery) == "UNKNOWN"

    def missing_recomputed(x):
        x["cases"].pop(0)
        recompute_metrics(x)
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "missing case with recomputed metrics", missing_recomputed)

    def duplicate_recomputed(x):
        x["cases"].append(deepcopy(x["cases"][0]))
        recompute_metrics(x)
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "duplicate id", duplicate_recomputed)

    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "wrong retrieval-list type", lambda x: x["cases"][5].__setitem__("candidate_retrieved_ids", "none"))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "missing critical flag", lambda x: x["cases"][0].pop("critical"))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "wrong document reference", lambda x: x["cases"][0].__setitem__("candidate_retrieved_ids", ["DOC-NOT-THERE"]))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "mismatched experiment", lambda x: x["experiments"]["index_only"]["runs"][1].__setitem__("retrieved_ids", ["DOC-ACCESS-02"]))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "Boolean count", lambda x: x["metrics"]["aggregate"]["candidate"].__setitem__("numerator", True))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "evidence overlap", lambda x: x["cases"][0]["forbidden"].append(x["cases"][0]["expected"][0]))
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "unsupported result evidence", lambda x: x["cases"][0].__setitem__("candidate", "Unlisted result"))

    def wrong_critical_membership(x):
        x["cases"][0]["critical"] = True
        recompute_metrics(x)
    expect_reject(FIXTURE, "critical membership", wrong_critical_membership)

    print(f"aggregate baseline {aggregate_b[0]}/{aggregate_b[1]}")
    print(f"aggregate candidate {aggregate_c[0]}/{aggregate_c[1]}")
    print(f"critical baseline {critical_b[0]}/{critical_b[1]}")
    print(f"critical candidate {critical_c[0]}/{critical_c[1]}")
    print("observed status BLOCKED")
    print(f"recovery aggregate {recovery_aggregate[0]}/{recovery_aggregate[1]}")
    print(f"recovery critical {recovery_critical[0]}/{recovery_critical[1]}")
    print("recovery release UNKNOWN")
    print("negative tests passed")
    print("all assertions passed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_tests()

sections.title: Assumptions, authority limits, and omitted evidence
paragraphs: ASSUMPTIONS. The four documents, corpus, cases, component identifiers, dates, traces, result strings, thresholds, controlled experiments, independent task, and recovery fixture are fictional teaching inputs. C-102 and C-103 are the declared critical accessibility slice. Pass and fail mean only the strict exact-string rule implemented in the exercise. The authored model identifier is a trace label and does not imply a capability, provider, or independently executed model. No production deployment, policy authority, operational owner, privacy approval, or release approval is assumed.

OMITTED. No real production evaluation, authoritative full policy set, live source-authority review, live source-freshness verification, privacy result, grader-calibration result, latency measurement, cost measurement, telemetry-reliability result, or production-shaped smoke-test result was supplied. These remain UNKNOWN and would require authorized records, authoritative policy review, calibrated evaluation, and controlled operational checks. The Python output is labeled expected until orchestrator execution. Therefore, neither the authored recovery replay nor this material establishes a production fix or an overall release PASS.
